residue.text: Unresolved supplied mechanism: agitation-generated optical disturbance could trigger continued agitation and renew disturbances. This return loop and bubble entrainment are hypotheses. Specks could instead be reflections or undissolved dye; neither their identity nor causal contribution is established. The selected construction does not require resolving them.

Supplied alternative omitted from the selected repeats: hypothetically compare enabled optical control at 900 rpm with a predetermined 60-second 900 rpm run, logging the rule in shadow mode and stopping both by second 105. Less stirring with both final targets met would support a costly feedback dependency; timer failure with enabled success would favor useful additional mixing. Different quiet durations limit attribution. This is an alternative allocation within six trials, not additional trials.

Supplied alternative omitted from the selected repeats: fixed 60-second 300/900 rpm pairs could test the hypothesized agitation-to-image arrow through matched moving and stopped observations. If capacity remains, reverse speed order and pause both at seconds 45–50, stopping at 65 to preserve 60 stirring seconds. Rapid optical change would not identify bubbles or prove prior uniformity; settling, surface shape and persistent artifacts remain rivals. Record cessation and quiet intervals.

Preserved limitations: only one successful lower-speed trial exists; matched 900 rpm final samples and preferred total duration are absent, so comparative uniformity and time savings remain unknown. Sampling can disturb gradients. Reference repeatability is not concentration calibration; commanded rpm lacks independent verification. Limited replication cannot establish general reliability. Other recipes, viscosities, vessels and continuous processes remain untested; no real chemical or human benefit is established.

summary.text: Retain the working hypothesis that fixed 300 rpm stirring for 60 seconds repeatedly meets the bounded final-vial criterion without optical stability. The stipulated 0.204, 0.209 and 0.207 readings, approximately 2.4 percent spread, counter universal necessity of sustained 900 rpm in this case. Repeatability and sufficiency remain hypotheses. Rival hypothesis: the successful trial was exceptional or sampling-mediated, and repeats retain gradients.

Proposed construction: allocate up to six fresh, rinsed-vessel repeats within 90 minutes; use 150 mL water, 0.30 mL dye, one bottle, fixed addition location and locked camera. Command 300 rpm for exactly 60 seconds, with no optical-driven restart. Log five-second side checks. Begin three 1 mL depth samples at second 120, finish within ten seconds and alternate sampling order. Use spill tray; stop if liquid escapes. Record references, raw samples, spread, duration and every failure. Predicted repeat success is spread at most 4 percent despite possible optical failures; repeated sample failures or order dependence favor the rival without proving 900 rpm necessary.
